text: I'll just start by saying Borderlands 2 is way better than the first. There's way, way more dialogue, a good story with a satisfying ending, good characters (note Tiny Tina, who is the best ADHD-infused character since Bart Simpson), a dickish but funny villian, varied environments, and a bazillion more guns. In this one you can choose from four brand new Vault Hunters, (and two more that the game developers added in later for an extra price, the cheeky buggers). You are on Pandora again, and have to quell its destruction by Handsome Jack, one of those villains you can't help but love.. to hate. And so you go off and do quests, gather things, defeat enemies, run back, level up your character etc. So yeah, the generic RPG elements are still there. But it does get awful addictive, doing quests and getting some nice loot and points. The environments are much more varied in this one, as apposed to just a Mad-Maxian desert. You start off on a cold glacier underneath a green Aurora, travel to grasslands, volcanoes spewing flames, purple mountains full of slag (a new purple element used in weapons and currency), and return to the deserts too. And there are way more enemies than just skags and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bandits this time. There is so much dialogue, in fact too much dialogue that can go over your head while you're concentrating on shooting the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of things around you. There's more in the first hour than there was in the whole of the first game. I think. The protagonists from the first game return as side characters, and even they speak more than they ever did before. it's nice to have allies speaking to you in a world where everything else is trying to kill you. Again there are literally millions of random guns and different loot strewn about; you never know what you're gonna get. You get some epic guns in the Sanctuary chest (which requires Gold keys; if you feel like cheating, people are giving them away every day . The game is most fun with four players, causing enough havoc and explosions to make Michael Bay tired. And it actually works this time! There's no Gamespy login ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t anymore. There's a lot of DLC. Too much DLC. So much it would make EA blush. You can get a Season Pass but it only covers like a quarter of the DLC released. You can get the Game of the Year edition but it still won't be enough. They honestly need to stop it, and release a Super Final Ultimate Edition which includes everything. Overall despite elements of the original still present, it's much improved and there's a whopping amount of varied content to get through. 9/10

title: borderlands: the pre-sequel
text: A much-needed change from Borderlands 2, and a welcome one in many places. It might not be better, but it's different, and that's what I wanted. Core game's Borderlands 2. Same UI, same shoot/loot gameplay, same levelling and such. It does however throw a lot of other stuff into the mix, which I'll quickly go over: The game no longer starts at the pace of Claptrap climbing stairs. You stand up next to a crashed rocket with two non-pitiful weapons and start shooting dudes. Action skill unlocks at level 2. The Grinder lets you "trade up" weapons to higher quality. I can get purples without tryharding for fifteen hours. I approve. The low gravity serves to make exploration a bit easier and allow ground slams, which are incredibly fun. Oz kits replace relics, which I thought were a bit underpowered in BL2, and they have all sorts of perks to take over the role, which I like. I didn't have issues with the oxygen mechanic, it makes things interesting getting from A to B, but I can see how some people might. Tip: Claptrap doesn't need air, if you can bare playing as him. TPS's 4-6 vault hunters are a bit niche for my tastes, with skills that seem to cater for very specific play styles, and if you choose the wrong one at the start you're out of luck. Their skills are however fresh and interesting, if of limited usefulness. Laser weapons, which come in varieties mimicking the other weapon types, are a bit uninspired, but whatever, lasers. Cryo damage freezes people in place and makes them take increased damage. Cryo replaces slag. It's like slag but cooler. That pun was unintentional. Enemies are about the same. There's a few new ones, like the swarming Torks and duplicate-on-death Kraggons, but most of the others are reskins or very close relatives to Borderlands' Bandits (Scavs), Hyperion Soldiers (Lost Legion), Buzzards (Dahl Fighters), etc. Also, stalkers for a single level! ASSET RECYCLING HO! This game also marks the triumphant return of the Eridian Guardians as enemies, which are some of my favourite baddies of all time, mostly because they and the places they spawn in look sick as hell. TPS really shines in the presentation. This game looks freaking The Elpian landscape, frozen, superheated, abandoned and bustling all at once, is more high-tech and futuristic than Pandora ever was. The Helios space-station's scale is unimaginable, not just from its eclipsing figure from Elpis, but when you get to explore its halls and facilities yourself later on. Fighting through all the areas that gave you grief in BL2, like the supply cannon and Jack's office, is awesome. Much later in the game, you once again delve into Eridian ruins, and holy hell, they look better than ever. The final area genuinely took my breath away. Look forward to it. It's also brillaint to be playing as the bad guys for once, and seeing the whole Borderlands scene from the other way around. The GUN Loaders are your allies. Helios Station is your base of operations. Wilhelm, Nisha and Athena all have actual personalities and react to things that happen in the world. I can finally appreciate the exquisite human being that is Jack without feeling guilty. Writing remains solid: Jack is tremendous as previously discussed, the characters catch you off guard with jokes, and the term "Paedophile mustache" is used unironically. Soundtrack is 99% retro sci-fi synths and it fits perfectly. Features the return of our lord and saviour Jesper Kyd. Praise be to his Nordic excellency. It's more Borderlands, as good as it was if not better. Just buy it and stop pretending you're not going to.

text: I absolutely loved the Borderlands series until this game. I picked up the original Borderlands by accident (I thought it was a different game; don't ask me how). After installing and playing it, I was absolutely absorbed. I bought the DLC's and enjoyed them thoroughly. When Borderlands 2 was announced, I watched the trailer at least 20 times over the course of a few months. I was so excited, and I rarely get excited about anything. BL2 is the only game I have ever preordered. It came out, I played it, and again I was sent into a euphoria. I played the DLCs one-by-one, as I had the season pass as well, and I was entertained for many hours. I will admit, I thought the Sir Hammerlock DLC kind of sucked, but the others were excellent. BL:TPS came out at a time I was really broke. I was not about to afford it until a Steam sale. I finally bought it and the season pass, not realizing what I was getting myself into. Pros: The humor and story was alright. I was compelled to actually respect Jack at first (not admire, but respect), and seeing him turn more and more into an evil mastermind. I also really enjoyed the variable gravity system, and butt-slamming my enemies was highly satisfying. The list unfortunately ends here. *SPOILER AHEAD* Cons: The first thing that really bugged me about this game was the raid boss. I realize that this is kind of late to finally realize I don't like this game, but I tried so hard to give it a chance. The raid boss is merely a slightly higher leveled final boss. This just seems very lazy to me. Another example of lazyness were the graphics. There was a pretty decent jump between BL1 and BL2, but seemingly no difference in graphics between BL2 and BL:TPS. I'm no gaming expert, so maybe there was a difference that I didn't notice. There were a number of other small things that bugged me, but the final thing that annoyed me, and this annoyed me the most, was the fact that there was only one DLC campaign instead of the four that BL1&2 had each, and there will be no more DLC after this. I just feel like I didn't get my money's worth, even if I bought it on sale. tl:dr - Don't buy this game unless it is super on sale. The game is way shorter than the other two, and there is only one campaign DLC, so don't let a good deal on the season pass fool you like it did me.

text: If you want a short description of the game play in "Botanicula," it's "random" and "arbitrary."  From that, you can probably guess that I'm not recommending the game.  Yes, as others have said, the visuals and sound are wonderful.  But, the game play is just silly.  In general, it consists of randomly clicking (or possibly dragging -- it's not obvious) on things on each screen a random number of times until a random and arbitrary thing results.  Randomly, you might have to repeat the above an arbitrary number of times until some other arbitrary things happen.  Also, be warned that you cannot go back to previous levels of the game without restarting.  So, if you manage to miss something optional (i.e., for an Achievement), happen to have everything necessary to finish the level, and click on the thing that finishes the level, you're SOL.  Using a walk-through, I managed to drag my way through level 4 of the game's 6 levels.  Looking at what was in level 5, I threw up my hands in disgust and quit (and I'm a completionist).  If you're one of the people who like other Amanita Design games, you'll probably love this one.  But, for the rest of us, just no.  Not Recommended.

text: Let me preface this by saying if you like puzzle games are have a sharp mind, you may want to check out Braid, and it's hard to say yes or no to whether I recommend this game, purely because it depends on who is looking at the product. I however, didn't have a great experience with it. I went into Braid after hearing a lot of hype and was really let down. Yes, the visuals are fantastic and beautiful, but some of the monster designs are just UGLY. The main enemy (out of only around 3 different varieties) just looks stupid, and another one is just a rabbit that makes a creepy noise before it jumps at you. Sound is alright, although I didn't really find any of the tracks incredibly great. They all do fine as ambience I suppose. Gameplay is alright. The main concept of time control is well executed, and the first world is pretty fair and rewarding. The difficulty has a very steep curve though and after a while the puzzles just seem overly complex and frustrating. Sadly each world is sort of independent of each other, and that's a shame. Instead of continually building off how you can use your powers, each world will basically introduce you to a new way of using your power or a new time concept. In one world, moving right moves time forward and left is backwards; in another you create shadow versions of yourself whenever you rewind time that will perform your old actions. This makes that in every world you have to master a completely new and mostly unrelated way of looking at puzzles. For some, this might be amazing and very rewarding, but as stated previously, the difficulty ramps up way too quick and things just get frustrating. Also, some hidden things are so hard to find you basically NEED to look up a walkthrough to get everything...I guarantee that 50% of people will have to restart the game due to a certain secret being hidden and locked away if you complex the puzzle from the first world. AWFUL design choice there. There's a bit of story that has apparently sparked a lot of discussion, but it didn't really grab me because it's put so separately from gameplay and told disjointedly. You'll basically have a few books you can read a wall of text from at the start of each world, but other than that there's nothing substantial. Whether or not you'll enjoy this game really depends on if you are a puzzle lover and critical thinker. If so, most of my review points probably won't affect you, and you won't get turned off by difficult puzzles. You can take more time to get into the story and I've heard that it is great if you do so, but it never really captured me. Check out a few gameplay videos before you purchase this game.

text: This isn't a bad game, it suffers from being overly hyped. Braid is very nice to look at, but I wouldn't say that everything is very well executed. The fact that certain mechanics are never given a decent explanation (i.e. what the arbitrary limitations are) makes a lot of this game very frustrating personally. I do like puzzles and games based around them, but there are too many times to me where the solutions have seemed "fiddly", for lack of a better word. You may understand the solution perfectly well, but it may be unnecessarily difficult, often due to the awkward platforming elements. All in all I have some enjoyable moments in the game, but I am very glad I got it on sale because this is simply not worth $10. The visuals are extremely polished, the gameplay could have used more work in my opinion. The underlying story is also boring me to tears.

title: braid
text: Gosh, what can I say about Braid? Post-modern narrative that integrates seamlessly with the puzzles you have to solve. One of the most beautiful gaming experiences I ever had, though I had to go online to figure out a few of the levels (the incredible simplicity of the systems had me give up faster than I normally do with games like this). The ending -- at least the one I got to (I was never able to complete the final challenge) was so insightful, I think I may have even shed a tear. My wife (non-gamer) and I played this together and had a wonderful time. Gameplay, graphics, music, story, absolutely everything. Highest recommendation.
